title: Make the help desk follow its own workflow

blocks.text: The help desk's tickets follow the support team's workflow:

rows: `CLOSED`, or back to `IN_PROGRESS` when the customer reopens it

blocks.text: Today the workflow lives only in a wiki page. Last week an agent's script moved a spam ticket from `CLOSED` straight to `IN_PROGRESS`, and the customer got a "we're working on it" email for a message they never sent. The agent's screen shows one button per allowed next state.
Finish the four `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Ticket.java`: the workflow table in `transitions()`, `canMoveTo(...)` and `allowedNext()` on `Ticket.State`, and `Ticket.moveTo(...)`.
When you're done, the workflow above is the only way a ticket moves, every state answers both questions, and nothing a screen does with its buttons changes the workflow. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: a ticket moves through every allowed step, including a reopen, and ends closed
a state answers which states may follow it
a closed ticket answers that it can move nowhere, without an exception
a change the workflow does not allow fails with IllegalStateException and the ticket keeps its state
changing the set of next states a caller received does not change the workflow

origin.section: A State Machine Keeps Its Transitions in an EnumMap Filled After the Constants Exist

concepts: A state machine keeps its allowed transitions in an EnumMap filled after the constants exist, refuses a move the table doesn't allow and keeps the old state, and gives terminal states an empty row.
